title: French Dip Roast Beef Sandwiches with Thyme Jus
summary: A salted beef joint is browned, roasted at 120 °C on a bed of onions to 63 °C and rested; the pan juices are simmered with stock into a jus, and the thinly sliced beef is dipped and piled into warm rolls.
equipment: ovenproof frying pan or roasting tin, about 30 cm
wire rack set in a tray
carving board and long sharp knife

ingredients.item: beef eye of round or topside roasting joint (halal), tied
fine sea salt or table salt
medium onion, halved and thinly sliced
crusty sub rolls, about 18 cm (about 420 g)

steps.title: Salt
steps.text: Salt the beef and rest it at least 1 hour.

steps.title: Brown
steps.text: Brown the joint on all sides in a hot pan.

steps.title: Build the base
steps.text: Soften the onion in butter, then stir in flour, tomato paste, thyme and garlic.

steps.title: Roast
steps.text: Roast at 120 °C on the onions until the centre reads 63 °C, then rest 20 minutes.

steps.title: Make the jus
steps.text: Simmer the pan contents with stock 10-15 minutes.

steps.title: Slice and dip
steps.text: Slice the beef very thinly, dip in the jus and fill the warm rolls; serve with jus on the side.

tips: Low-temperature roasting keeps the joint evenly pink.
Slice as thinly as you can; a cold joint slices thinnest.
A low-salt stock keeps the jus from getting too salty as it reduces.
storage: Refrigerate the beef and jus separately within 1 hour for up to 3 days; reheat the jus to a boil and dip the beef until hot. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
